title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Vector Space Model — TF-IDF & Cosine Similarity
summary: The Vector Space Model (VSM) represents documents and queries as vectors in a high-dimensional term space (one dimension per unique vocabulary term). Each dimension's value is the TF-IDF weight of the corresponding term.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body:
The Vector Space Model (VSM) represents documents and queries as vectors in a high-dimensional term space (one dimension per unique vocabulary term). Each dimension's value is the TF-IDF weight of the corresponding term. Relevance is measured as cosine similarity between the query vector and each document vector, making it scale-invariant with respect to document length. VSM enables ranking (unlike Boolean), supports partial matching, and is geometrically interpretable. The key insight is that documents and queries occupy the same vector space, and angular proximity implies topical similarity.

$$\text{cosine}(q, d) = \frac{q \cdot d}{|q| \cdot |d|} = \frac{\sum_{t} w_{t,q} \cdot w_{t,d}}{\sqrt{\sum_t w_{t,q}^2} \cdot \sqrt{\sum_t w_{t,d}^2}}$$

quiz.question: Why use cosine similarity rather than dot product in VSM?
options: Given a static document collection and a new query, retrieve the most relevant documents.
An inverted index maps each unique term to a list (posting list) of document IDs where that term appears, with optional frequency and position data.
Maximum likelihood over the entire corpus: P(t|C) = total_count(t) / total_tokens.
Dot product favours longer documents because they have larger magnitude vectors.
quiz.explanation: Dot product favours longer documents because they have larger magnitude vectors. Cosine normalises by vector magnitude, making similarity length-invariant. Score reflects angle, not magnitude.

options: Databases retrieve exact matches on structured data with SQL.

/n or NEAR(n) — requires two terms to appear within n positions of each other.
Either TF=0 (term doesn't appear in the document) or IDF=0 (term appears in every document and is thus useless for discrimination).
quiz.explanation: Either TF=0 (term doesn't appear in the document) or IDF=0 (term appears in every document and is thus useless for discrimination). Both cases correctly give a weight of 0.
